Subject: Rate card + competitor pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Hi Dylan,

Quick intro — I lead platform procurement at Nimbus Labs. We're evaluating hosted inference for our product search ranking and personalization pipelines. Before we set up a demo, can you send your current hosted API rate card and a short comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS?

High-level requirements:
- Steady-state: ~350M tokens/month (text gen + few-shot reranking)
- Burst: up to 1B tokens in promotional periods
- Need enterprise SLAs (uptime + data controls) and SOC2 evidence

Specifically interested in: baseline token pricing (input/output), embedding pricing, any volume tiers/committed discounts, and whether Redwood will match/beat quoted competitor unit pricing for a multi-quarter commitment.

If you can share a one-pager + ballpark numbers today that'd be great — procurement will want to see line items.

Thanks,
Carmen Ruiz
VP, Engineering Operations
Nimbus Labs

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate card + competitor pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Hi Carmen — thanks for the note and the clear requirements. Looping in Laura (your account exec) who will help with the commercial proposal.

Attached is our hosted API rate card (Redwood-Hosted-Ratecard-Q3.pdf) and a short competitive snapshot we maintain. Quick highlights (ballpark):
- Base text generation: $0.0007 / input token, $0.0014 / output token for the curated Llama-family models we host.
- Embeddings: $0.0002 / embedding (per 1k-vector unit equivalent) — volume tiers reduce to $0.00012 at >200M embeddings/month.
- Large-volume committed tiers: we offer 15–30% off list depending on commitment and term; additional custom pricing possible for strategic partners.

We generally benchmark vs OpenAI and Anthropic. For reference, customers we spoke with reported OpenAI list at ~ $0.002 / output token for similar workloads (chat style), Anthropic varies by model family. Together/AWS often compete on committed discounts if they're bundling infra.

Would love to understand the competitor quotes you have so we can be explicit about matching. Can you share the line-items (token price, term, any add-on fees) from the competing offer? If you prefer, we can also propose a provisional match for the volumes you called out and make a mutual action plan.

Attaching: Redwood-Hosted-Ratecard-Q3.pdf, Competitive-Comparison-OpenAI-Anthropic.xlsx

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[dylan.brooks@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142]

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rate card + competitor pricing (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS)

Thanks Dylan — attaching the competitor quote we received. Key points:
- OpenAI (private offer): $0.0009 / input token, $0.0018 / output token; 12-month term; 20% discount applied to list for committed monthly volume of 400M tokens.
- Anthropic: slightly higher list; offered a migration credit but not a straight unit price match.
- AWS Bedrock/Together: bundling infra brings latency benefits but opaque unit economics in the quote we have.

Our procurement asks: can Redwood match OpenAI's effective unit price for output tokens ($0.0018) for the first year if Nimbus commits to a 12-month minimum and provides forecasted monthly volume? If not exact match, what's the closest you can get and what strings are attached (SLA credits, support tiers, egress fees, etc.)?

Attached: competitor-quote.pdf

Regards,
Carmen

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Nimbus Labs (NIM-2026-0610) — pricing match request / proposed MAP

Team — prospect asked us to match OpenAI effective output price $0.0018 for 12 months with a 400M token commit. Summary:
- Proposed Redwood baseline (from ratecard): $0.0007 input / $0.0014 output list.
- Prospect target: $0.0018 output (OpenAI effective after discount).
- Margins: at $0.0014 we're comfortable; at $0.0018 per output token they're actually paying more than our list, so matching is feasible only if we agree to additional commercial commitments (upfront, longer term, or add-on professional services).

Requesting quick guidance:
1) Laura — suggest commercial offer we present (tiered discount + 1-time onboarding credit?)
2) Rafael — do we have authority to offer an introductory match for Q3 for up to 6 months as a trial? If not, what's required for approval?
3) Neha — confirm if there are hidden infra costs for the bursts (1B tokens) and whether we should include burst caps or throttle language.

I've prepared a short Mutual Action Plan (NIM-MAP-2026.pdf) with milestones: PO, security review (SOC2 evidence — we've got standard pack), pilot start, commit start. Attaching it here.

Proposed quick offer to share with Carmen while we get approvals:
- 12-month contract, 400M committed monthly tokens.
- Redwood provides an effective output token price of $0.00175 for months 1–12 (slight discount under OpenAI effective).
- One-time onboarding credit of $25k (applied to first invoice).
- SLA: 99.9% uptime, standard support; SOC2 report provided.
- Burst allowance: additional tokens billed at list with an agreed burst cap; negotiate for 2x monthly for promo periods.

Happy to iterate — low-friction ask from prospect.

Thanks,
Dylan

[Attachment: NIM-MAP-2026.pdf]

All — good thread. Approve the customer-facing offer with two conditions:
1) Finance sign-off (Priyom) on the onboarding credit and the 1.75c output effective price for the first 12 months; ensure modeled gross margin remains >=18% over expected volume.
2) Legal to accept the burst cap language in the MAP; if procurement pushes higher burst caps, tie to a staged pricing step-up for any tokens beyond 2x committed monthly.

Priyom: please fast-track margin calc and confirm whether accounting needs the onboarding credit amortized over the year for revenue recognition.
Laura/Dylan: share the proposed customer email and the MAP; I'll approve the external send once I see finance thumbs-up.
Neha: confirm any infra/ops limits for a 1B burst and any recommended guardrails.
